summary: Phase 2 per-app CD workflows pass Review A on the re-review at 1902a8215. The delta since the prior Review A head 09ce375d2 holds the Red r5 to r8 test commits, Green r3 (runbook tag lookup and action pins), Green r4 (the matrix substitutions field), and the strategy and plan commits; no other commit touched a phase path. The select-step substitutions logic is correct: marketing alone holds exactly one REQUIRED_ default and receives the pushed commit; sales holds three REQUIRED_ defaults and stays the recorded open limit; a missing push file yields an empty field and the submit fails closed; the two select steps stay equal after trim. The four action pins match their tags, and the version comments are right. The runbook names the real services, regions, and projects of the table. The Red edits of the old tests in the six apps keep every check. No Green commit touched a test file. The independent runs match the plan claims: the scripts/ci suite and the storytime guard files pass 119 tests (107 plus 12), and the sales guard line fails only on the known approval case (28 passed, 1 failed). Four Nits remain; none blocks the phase.
nonblocking_findings: A31 [Nit] test-strategy.md: the storytime guard row records 'the r5 app count is 17 passed across 3 files', but the command of the same row names 2 files that hold 12 tests, and the gate runs measured 12 passed; the codecamp row records '133 tests: 131 passed' while the measured gate run gives 86 passed, 2 failed, 47 skipped. The stale Red r5 counts mislead a reader of the strategy. Rationale: the operative gate criteria are '0 failed', known_failures=4, other_failures=0, and sales 28 passed 1 failed; they are unambiguous and hold, and the Green log records the mismatch honestly. The phase gate does not read the stale numbers. Owner: user or build session (a one-line strategy amendment).

A32 [Nit] commit 4f4a89337: the storytime Red r5 commit holds no reason line in its body. The reason ('Read gcloud run deploy from the bash script and keep every check') sits only in the Red r5 log table. The other five app-test commits (e8917df46, b5087acbe, c934643b5, a987ccb48, 7cc94da8a) carry the reason in the body. Rationale: the R-EDIT convention of the framework asks for a one-line reason in the commit body when Red edits an old test. The edit itself keeps every old assertion and adds a no-update-traffic check, so the test strength is intact.

A33 [Nit] scripts/ci/__tests__/cd-workflows.test.mjs: no committed case runs the select step against a push file, so the substitutions regex of the select step is never exercised with the real cloudbuild files. The W-05 dry runs build scratch repositories that hold no push file (realPlanFiles copies the manifests, the table, and the script only), so the field is always the empty string in the committed runs. The marketing behavior is proven by the Green r4 dry render (logged, not committed) and by the W-24 artifact check, which parses the YAML. Rationale: the regex matches the exact text '^  (_[A-Z0-9_]+): "REQUIRED_' with a 2-space indent and double quotes; a formatting change of apps/marketing/cloudbuild.yaml would silently drop the substitution and fail the marketing build at validate-release-inputs. The failure is closed, so the severity is Nit. A future case should copy the push file of each gated row into the scratch repository and assert the field value.

A34 [Nit] scripts/ci/__tests__/cd-workflows.test.mjs: W-23 pins the 40-hex SHA form of every uses: line (uses_lines=10) but never checks the trailing version comment. A missing or wrong comment passes the case, while contract C23 asks for the version in a trailing comment. Rationale: all four comments are correct today (checkout v4.4.0 = 11d5960a..., setup-node v4.4.0 = 49933ea5..., auth v2.1.13 = c200f369..., setup-gcloud v2.2.1 = e427ad8a..., verified against the upstream tags), and a comment check is a hermetic text check, so the gap is small.
evidence: Provenance: git rev-parse HEAD returned 1902a8215299d96c4079fb877d38b351eb1f7c55, which equals the supplied audited HEAD 1902a8215 and the role_base_sha. git log with --name-only over 09ce375d2..1902a8215 on the phase paths (.github/workflows, scripts/ci, docs/runbooks, the nine cloudbuild push and traffic files, and the ten guard test files) lists exactly the scoped commits: Red r5 (4f4a89337, e8917df46, b5087acbe, c934643b5, a987ccb48), Red r6 (85ad8bb87), Red r7 (7cc94da8a), Red r8 (8380479ea), Green r3 (3f1c33b9a, a60c8352c, 688a2abb2), Green r4 (bbe334bff, d19c603d0, 1902a8215), plus the strategy commits 5387596c2 and 03085e260 and the plan commit 9e10c5bad. No commit of another track touched a phase path in the range.

Independent run (this review, foreground, through heavy-run.sh): 'CI=true pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=1 scripts/ci apps/storytime/__tests__/phase1-service.test.ts apps/storytime/__tests__/phase3-media-gate.test.ts' gave EXIT=0, Test Files 6 passed (6), Tests 119 passed (119). The arithmetic matches the plan claims for the two parts run separately: 4 files with 107 tests for scripts/ci plus 2 files with 12 tests for the storytime guard line. A failure in either part would have failed the combined run.

Sales guard line (this review, foreground, through heavy-run.sh): EXIT=1, Test Files 1 failed | 3 passed (4), Tests 1 failed | 28 passed (29). The single failure is 'seeds only deterministic approved curriculum and gates exact completeness' on releaseCandidate.approval (status awaiting_human_review, evidenceSha256 null, reviewer null), which is known failure item 4 of the strategy and matches the Green r4 gate and the plan note (28 passed, 1 known failure).

Select-step substitutions logic (bbe334bff): the regex /^  (_[A-Z0-9_]+): "REQUIRED_/gm reads the push file of each affected gated row. Measured over the real files: apps/marketing/cloudbuild.yaml holds exactly one REQUIRED_ default (_RELEASE_COMMIT_SHA), so its matrix entry receives --substitutions=_RELEASE_COMMIT_SHA=<HEAD_SHA>; the sales push file holds three (_RELEASE_COMMIT_SHA, _CURRICULUM_BACKUP_NOT_BEFORE, _RELEASE_SOURCE_MANIFEST_SHA256), so the only-_RELEASE_COMMIT_SHA rule is false and the field stays empty, which is the open limit the runbook records; the other gated rows hold none, so the field is empty. A missing file returns the empty string through the existsSync guard, the row still enters the matrix, and the submit fails closed on the missing config. HEAD_SHA comes from the step env github.sha, so no injection reaches the command. The empty matrix field leaves a bare line-continuation in the submit script, which bash accepts.

W-18c equality holds: the two select run: blocks of cd-apps.yml and cd-www-reading-advantage.yml are identical text (the case trims both and asserts non-empty and equal; it passed in the 107). The www deploy job ignores the matrix, and the www=yes|no output is unchanged, so the copy in the www workflow is harmless.

Action pins (a60c8352c): both workflows pin 10 uses: lines (5 each) to four 40-hex SHAs with version comments. Live re-check: git ls-remote https://github.com/actions/checkout.git refs/tags/v4.4.0 returned 11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 refs/tags/v4.4.0, which equals the pinned SHA of the comment '# v4.4.0'. The orchestrator's ls-remote of 2026-11-07 confirmed the other three: setup-node v4.4.0 = 49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020, google-github-actions/auth v2.1.13 = c200f3691d83b41bf9bbd8638997a462592937ed, google-github-actions/setup-gcloud v2.2.1 = e427ad8a34f8676edf47cf7d7925499adf3eb74f. Each tag is a lightweight tag on a commit, so the SHA is the commit. All four comments are correct.

Runbook tag lookup (3f1c33b9a): the six sections of docs/runbooks/traffic-moves.md name the real service, region asia-southeast1, and project, and they match scripts/ci/apps.json and the measured facts M41 and M42: primary-advantage-app in primary-advantage; accounts, accounting, codecamp-advantage, marketing, sales-advantage in reading-advantage. The tag shapes match the table (pa- and ac- and c prefixes, candidate, sso-candidate, legacy-rollback and candidate). The sales section names _PUSH_BUILD_ID and the three REQUIRED inputs; the sales traffic file uses ${_PUSH_BUILD_ID} for the capture image and --to-tags=candidate=100, and holds the three REQUIRED defaults with no default for _PUSH_BUILD_ID. The Open limits bullet states the marketing and sales substitution state exactly as the code behaves.

Red edits keep their strength: the diffs of 4f4a89337 (storytime phase1-service reads the gcloud run deploy command from the bash step and keeps every old assertion plus a new no-update-traffic check), e8917df46 (db: three files re-pointed to the traffic file, anchored on update-traffic, with a new push-file no-DB assertion), b5087acbe (accounting), c934643b5 (accounts), a987ccb48 (marketing), and 7cc94da8a (sales: push and traffic order lists, the counts over the combined text kept, and six new push-file no-DB assertions) all keep or increase the checks. No check was deleted or loosened.

No test file changed after its Red commit in a Green commit: git show --stat of 3f1c33b9a (two runbooks), a60c8352c (two workflows), 688a2abb2, d19c603d0, 1902a8215 (plan.md only), and bbe334bff (two workflows plus traffic-moves.md) shows no path under scripts/ci/__tests__ or any app test directory. No dependency file changed, and no out-of-scope path appears.

A3: the new cases W-22 to W-26 label every count (sections_checked=6, uses_lines, rows_checked, required_rows, changed_files) and the plan notes quote labeled counts. No bare-digit count was found in the delta. A4: W-22 asserts sections.length===6 before the loop; W-23 asserts lines>=5 before the verdict; W-24 asserts rows.length>=1, needs.length>=1, and that marketing is among the needs; W-25 asserts 4 rows before the loop; W-26 asserts the sales row exists. Red r6 proved W-22 and W-23 fail at the base, and Red r8 proved W-24 fails at the base with scratch fixtures that pass and fail as designed, so no new case is vacuous. A5: the plan r4 claims (107 passed, storytime 12 passed, sales 28 passed 1 known failure, known_failures=4) match this review's independent runs; no claim of a passing command contradicts an actual exit.

Storytime guard row judged: the strategy row's command names 2 files (phase1-service.test.ts and phase3-media-gate.test.ts) that hold 12 tests (3 plus 9, one looped over three parts). This review ran the command and got 12 passed, 0 failed, EXIT=0, which satisfies the row's operative criterion '0 failed' and the phase criteria known_failures=4 and other_failures=0. The recorded 'r5 app count is 17 passed across 3 files' contradicts the command of its own row and the measured 12; it is stale Red r5 data, recorded as finding A31, not a gate failure.

Re-review scope: no CONTEST item was routed to Review A. The prior Review A result (review-a-09ce375d2.json) passed with three nonblocking notes (N1 sales capture-script first-run limit, N2 evidence class, N3 combined Green run); the remediation rounds of this delta came from Review B finding B1 (IAM, fixed outside the repository) and Review C finding B1 (runbook tag lookup, fixed by 3f1c33b9a). N1 remains accurate and stays recorded in the runbook Open limits; nothing to withdraw or keep.
